messages:
Alex Chen: Quick check on Deployments create/delete UX. Sketches in Figma: https://www.figma.com/file/abcd1234/Deployments-forms (frames 5-8). Proposal: show inline validation for actionable fields, surface a compact error summary at top for submit/server errors, label required fields with the word 'Required' (not only *), and add stricter delete confirmations for prod (type-to-confirm). Looking for tradeoffs and a11y concerns.

Priya Shah: I like inline for immediate feedback but worried about clutter on narrow screens. Can we defer inline hints until field blur or only after first submit? Also +1 on explicit 'Required' instead of just an asterisk.

Jamal Ortiz: Engineering prefers inline-on-blur. From API side we need stable error shapes like { location: 'field'|'form', field: 'name', message: '...' } so the client can attach messages and focus. For global errors, top summary with anchor links is fine.

Emily Ruiz: Accessibility considerations: connect error text to inputs via aria-describedby and ensure critical errors are announced (role="alert" or aria-live). For required fields add visible 'Required' and add screen-reader-only text "This field is required". Modal dialogs should trap focus and announce when opened.

Robin Park: Implementation plan: extend FormField with props: errorText, requiredLabel:boolean, showInlineOn: 'blur'|'submit'|'always'. Add data-error-anchor ids so the top summary can link/focus. I'll prototype a component-level solution and include tests for keyboard + screen reader behavior.

Alex Chen: On delete confirmations: current modal "Are you sure?" is weak. Proposal: tiered confirmations: simple confirm for non-prod, type-to-confirm for deployments marked production or with > threshold traffic, include explicit consequences and a link to audit logs. Want to avoid overburdening users but prevent accidental prod deletes.

Priya Shah: Strongly prefer tiering. Forcing type-to-confirm everywhere is annoying. Copy: show the resource name, consequences (irreversible), and a clear affordance to cancel. Keep the destructive button label explicit: 'Delete deployment <name>' and make it red.

Emily Ruiz: For the type-to-confirm pattern: label the input (not only placeholder), provide screen-reader instructions, and ensure keyboard users can cancel easily. When modal opens announce via live-region: 'Delete deployment modal opened.' For prod type-to-confirm, require exact match to enable button; still allow Escape to cancel.

Jamal Ortiz: Engineering caveat: disabling Escape can break muscle memory. Better to keep Escape to cancel and only enable the destructive action after exact typed match. Also surface focus_hint boolean from API errors so client can focus intended field after render.

Robin Park: I'll create branch r/feat/form-validation-patterns with: FormField updates, top-error-summary component, modal variants (simple vs typed confirm), aria-live announcements, and unit/e2e tests. Will tag UX and A11y for reviews.

Alex Chen: Great. Priya & Emily please review the Figma frames and the PR when ready. Paste copy changes into Figma comments. Thanks! :thumbsup:
